notes: The skill's value shows most clearly in eval 2 (guided-handoff): without the skill, Claude performs a good review and shows handoff commands, but the implementation agent prompt is generic and doesn't carry forward the review findings. With the skill, review notes are explicitly bridged into the agent prompt as implementation guidance.

Evals 1 and 3 pass 100% in both configurations — Claude naturally handles standalone review and full automation well. The skill adds structure (checkbox format, mode-calibrated expectations) but both configurations meet the assertions.
Token overhead is ~18% (21.4k vs 18.2k mean) — the skill's structured review template adds context but the increase is modest. Time overhead is ~7% (101s vs 95s mean).

The single discriminating assertion ('Includes review notes or implementation guidance for the agent') is the strongest signal for the skill's value: it ensures review findings don't get lost in the handoff to the implementation agent.
